entries.title: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure and charters out tankers into October, sources say
entries.claimSummary: QatarEnergy extended force majeure for LNG supplies to several Asian buyers into mid-September.
extractedFacts: Force-majeure notices due to expire in August and early September were extended until mid-September.
Affected buyers include customers in South Korea, India and Bangladesh.
QatarEnergy continued leasing some LNG tankers through mid-October.
At least nine QELM/QET-controlled LNG carriers were sub-chartered to named third parties.
entries.carryReason: No newer source-verified QatarEnergy force-majeure notice was approved in the Aug 18 review; the Reuters July 23 notice extending force majeure through mid-September remains the latest approved disclosure, with the mid-October extension still unconfirmed preparation.

entries.title: Strait of Hormuz Crossings Rise 8% Week-on-Week, But Dark AIS Activity Remains Elevated
entries.claimSummary: Kpler vessel-type data reported via Foreign Policy Journal shows 3 LNG tanker transits among 106 total Hormuz crossings during Jul 27-Aug 2, the first LNG-specific movement since the carried July 18 zero-transit observation.
extractedFacts: The week of Jul 27-Aug 2 recorded 106 total crossings by 96 distinct vessels, up 8% from 98 crossings the prior week.
Vessel-type breakdown of the 106 crossings included 3 LNG tankers, 40 liquid tankers, 24 bulk carriers, and smaller counts of other vessel types.
Dark AIS activity (undetermined routes) covered 41% of crossings, down from 49% the prior week.
entries.carryReason: No newer source-verified weekly Kpler LNG-transit breakdown was approved in the Aug 18 review; the Aug 3 Foreign Policy Journal count of 3 LNG transits for the week of Jul 27-Aug 2 remains the latest approved figure.

entries.title: Ship traffic through Strait of Hormuz near three-month low
entries.publisher: Investing.com (via Yahoo Finance UK, citing Kpler)
entries.claimSummary: An Investing.com report carried by Yahoo Finance UK on Aug 13, citing Kpler data, said Hormuz vessel transits averaged 13/day over the five days to Aug 11, about 90% below the pre-war 130/day baseline and approaching the lowest level since May 12.
extractedFacts: Kpler data showed vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz averaging approximately 13 ships per day over the five-day period ending Tuesday, Aug 11.
Current traffic levels are approximately 90% below the daily average of 130 ships that passed through Hormuz before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28.
The current 7-day average oil export volume was approximately 9 million barrels per day, versus a pre-conflict volume of approximately 20 million barrels per day.

Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority posted on X that claims the strait has reopened 'do not change the reality: the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked and will not be reopened until Iran's conditions are accepted.'
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said private businesses undercount the number of ships leaving the Strait of Hormuz due to ships moving covertly through the waterway.
entries.carryReason: AP reported limited traffic but did not provide a comparable current five-day average; no newer source-verified Kpler daily/5-day-average figure was approved on Aug 18. Retain the Aug 13 Kpler-sourced figure of 13/day through Aug 11.

extractedFacts: A projectile damaged a ship's engine room as it sailed out of Hormuz off Oman on Aug 18 and caused a crew casualty; responsibility was not claimed.
AP reported Trump threatened to bomb Oman because he opposed parts of the near-term Iranian-Omani route-management arrangement.
Iranian officials said the strait would not reopen until the United States met its conditions.
